(a) Yearly Social Security for the household: none / $1 to $10,000 / $10,000 to $20,000 / $20,000 to $30,000 / $30,000 or more
(b) Yearly other income (pensions, unemployment, interest, child support): none / $1 to $5,000 / $5,000 to $15,000 / $15,000 or more
(c) Bank accounts and investments: under $2,000 / $2,000 to $5,000 / $5,000 to $20,000 / $20,000 to $100,000 / $100,000 or more
(d) Is your father part of your household (yes/no)? If yes, does he get any income?

summary: Pennsylvania household; answers were inconsistent (household described as "just me" but a 72-year-old father is said to live with you). Reported about $30,000/year income (source unclear), $140,000 to $200,000 in assets (unclear whether this is savings/investments or home value), no one working, you own your home, no children, no employer insurance, no disability. Likely SNAP (income near the gross limit; the asset test is generally waived in PA) and ACA premium tax credit (no employer coverage, income above Medicaid limits). Not recommended: SSI (asset limit of $2,000 likely exceeded, and not 65+ or disabled as stated), TANF (assets and no children), Medicaid (income above limit unless household is different), CHIP, WIC, school meals, CTC, EITC (no children and no earned income). A caseworker should confirm household composition, the income source and amount, and whether the $140k to $200k is liquid savings, since that could change results.
